units.Ezra 10:4: Arise, for the matter rests upon you, and we are with you. Be strong and act.”

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel formation associated with the womb and commission toward nations
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah is known and consecrated before birth and appointed a prophet to nations. Isaiah describes one formed from the belly as God's servant and appointed a light for nations, sharing vocation associated with formation and an international scope without identifying the two speakers.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Before I formed you in the belly, I know you; before you came out of the womb, I have consecrated you. I have appointed you a prophet to nations.

target_units.text: And now thus says the Lord, who formed me from the belly as His slave to gather Jacob and Israel to Him—I will be gathered and glorified before the Lord, and my God will be my strength—

and He said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called My servant, to establish Jacob’s tribes and bring back Israel’s dispersion. Behold, I have appointed you as a covenant for a race, a light for nations, so that you may bring salvation to the earth’s extremity.”

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel fearless delivery of God's words despite hostile hearers
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah must rise, speak everything commanded and not fear his opponents. Ezekiel similarly receives the command not to fear hostile faces or words and to deliver God's words to the embittering house.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: But you, gird your waist, rise and tell them everything I command you. Do not fear them or be terrified before them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.

target_units.text: And you, son of man, do not fear them or be shaken before their faces, because they will rage and gather against you all around, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be shaken before their faces, for it is an embittering house.
You will speak My words to them, if indeed they listen or are terrified, for it is an embittering house.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel designation of Israel as holy to God
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah calls Israel holy to the Lord. Exodus describes covenant-keeping Israel as God's treasured people and a holy nation, providing a covenant counterpart to that sacred status.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Israel is holy. To the Lord he is the first of His produce. All who devour him will offend; calamities will come upon them, declares the Lord.

target_units.text: Now therefore, if you diligently listen to My voice, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the sons of Israel.”

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: shared firstfruits imagery for people belonging to God
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah calls Israel the first of the Lord's produce. James calls those born through the word of truth a kind of firstfruits of God's creatures; the shared agricultural imagery is clear, while the target does not repeat Jeremiah's warning against devouring Israel.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Israel is holy. To the Lord he is the first of His produce. All who devour him will offend; calamities will come upon them, declares the Lord.

target_units.text: By His will He gave us birth through the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel indictment of corrupt civil and religious leadership
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah indicts several leadership groups, including law handlers who do not know God and prophets who speak by Baal. Micah similarly indicts leaders, priests and prophets, specifying distorted justice and paid religious service rather than Jeremiah's particular Baal charge.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: The priests did not say, Where is the Lord? Those holding to the law did not know Me; the shepherds acted ungodly toward Me; the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed what is useless.

target_units.text: Hear these things now, leaders of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house, who abhor justice and twist all straight things,
you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustices!

Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel exchange of glory for futile worship
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah says God's people exchanged their glory and will derive no benefit. The psalm specifies the exchange of their glory for the likeness of a grass-eating calf and the forgetting of their saving God.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Will nations exchange their gods, though these are not gods? But My people exchanged their glory, from which they will not benefit.

target_units.text: They made a calf at Horeb and bowed down to a carved image.
They exchanged their glory for the likeness of a calf that eats grass.
They forgot the God who saved them, who did great things in Egypt,

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: related heavenly witness to Israel's rejection of God
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah portrays heaven as astonished and shuddering at the people's exchange. Isaiah summons heaven and earth to hear the Lord's charge that His children rejected and abandoned Him; the cosmic response differs from the summons to witness.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Heaven was astonished at this and shuddered exceedingly, says the Lord.

target_units.text: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel pursuit of other lovers despite warning or obstruction
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah's woman answers the warning about her road and thirst with I will be strong, and the text says she loved strangers and followed them. Hosea's mother likewise declares that she will follow lovers, whose pursuit is then obstructed; the eventual return in Hosea is not asserted of Jeremiah's speaker.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Turn your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, I will be strong, because she had loved strangers and went after them.

target_units.text: For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’
Therefore look, I block her way with thorns and will build up her roads, and she will certainly not find her path.

She will pursue her lovers but certainly not catch them; she will seek them but certainly not find them. She will say, ‘I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better for me then than now.’

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: legal contrast distinguishing innocent blood from a fatal break-in
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah charges bloodshed against innocent lives and explicitly says they were not found in break-ins. Exodus excludes murder in the death of a thief found breaking in and then distinguishes a case after sunrise; this supplies a legal contrast without resolving the target's later pronouns or Jeremiah's oak detail.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Even on your hands was found the blood of innocent lives. I did not find them in break-ins, but at every oak.

target_units.text: “And if the thief is found breaking in, and is struck and dies, there is no murder in his case.
But if the sun has risen upon him, he is guilty; he shall die in return. And if he has nothing, let him be sold for the theft.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: legal background to the divorce and remarriage question
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah asks whether a dismissed wife who becomes another man's will return to her former husband, before confronting the people's many shepherds. Deuteronomy forbids the former husband from taking such a wife back after the intervening marriage, supplying the stated legal analogy rather than resolving all the prophetic question's implications.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s, surely she will not return to him again? Would not that woman be utterly polluted? And you prostituted yourself with many shepherds—and were you returning to Me? says the Lord.

target_units.text: And if a man takes a wife and dwells with her as husband, and she finds no favour in his sight, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house,
and she departs and becomes another man’s wife,

and the latter husband hates her, and writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her to be his wife dies,

her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled; for it is an abomination before the Lord your God. And you shall not defile the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel roadside prostitution imagery for covenant infidelity
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah portrays the woman seated on roads and polluting the land through prostitution. Ezekiel's address to Jerusalem describes prostitution chambers in broad streets and at road heads, giving a particular counterpart to the public locations without reproducing the solitary-crow image.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Lift your eyes straight ahead and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat for them on the roads like a solitary crow, and polluted the land with your prostitution and your evils.

target_units.text: you built yourself a prostitution chamber and made yourself a display place in every broad street,
and at the head of every road you built your brothels, ruined your beauty, spread your legs to every passerby, and multiplied your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel trumpet alarm addressed to Zion's region
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah commands a trumpet signal and loud warning in Judah and Jerusalem as people gather toward walled cities. Joel similarly commands the trumpet in Zion and proclamation on the holy mountain, explaining the alarm through the announced Lord's day.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!

target_units.text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel threat from distant forces
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah announces bands from a distant land raising their voice against Judah's cities. Isaiah likewise describes a signal among distant nations and their rapid, armed arrival, giving the military counterpart to the distant bands.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Remind the nations: Behold, they have come! Announce in Jerusalem: Bands come from a distant land and have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.

target_units.text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!
They will not hunger or grow weary, slumber or sleep, nor loosen the belts from their waists; their sandal straps will certainly not break.
Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.
They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: contrast between skill in evil and wisdom in goodness
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah calls the leaders of the people wise at evil but untrained in doing good. Paul desires the opposite orientation: wisdom about good and innocence about evil, furnishing a sharply reversed moral pattern.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.

target_units.text: For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel resistance to correction despite repeated punishment
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah says the people refuse instruction and refuse to return even after scourging and devastation. Amos likewise recounts destructive blows and repeatedly says that the people still did not turn to God.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Lord, Thine eyes are toward faithfulness. Thou didst scourge them, and they did not suffer; Thou broughtest them to an end, and they would not accept instruction. They hardened their faces beyond rock and would not return.

target_units.text: “I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

“I sent death among you on Egypt’s road and killed your young men with the sword, along with the captivity of your horses. I brought your camps up in fire in My anger; yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: same-chapter contrast between poor and prosperous people in disobedience
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: The speaker first considers people who may be poor and lack ability and knowledge of God's way. He then proposes going to prosperous people who recognized that way and judgment, yet reports that they broke the yoke too; the shared failure cuts across the stated contrast in means and knowledge.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: And I said: Perhaps they are poor, because they had no ability, because they did not know the Lord’s way and God’s judgment.

target_units.text: I will go to the prosperous and speak to them, for they recognized the Lord’s way and God’s judgment. And behold, with one accord they broke the yoke and tore the bonds.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel discipline opposed to the city's destruction
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah speaks of Jerusalem being instructed lest God's soul depart and it become uninhabitable. Zephaniah likewise indicts a city's refusal of discipline and reports a promise against destruction tied to fear of God and acceptance of discipline.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: you will be instructed, Jerusalem, lest My soul depart from you, lest I make you an impassable land that will not be inhabited.

target_units.text: She did not heed a voice or accept discipline; she did not trust the Lord or approach her God.
Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like Arabian wolves, leaving nothing for morning.
Her prophets are bearers of a spirit, contemptuous men; her priests profane holy things and act impiously toward law.

But the Lord is righteous within her and will certainly do no injustice. Morning by morning He will bring His judgment to light; He was not hidden and knew no injustice in exaction, nor injustice in strife.
In destruction I tore down the proud; their corners vanished. I will make their roads utterly desolate, with no passing through; their cities failed because no one existed or dwelt there.
I said, “Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will certainly not be destroyed from her eyes,” with all I exacted upon her. Prepare, rise early! All their gleaning has been ruined.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: repeated image of divine fury poured upon the land's inhabitants
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah 6 threatens an outpouring of fury across children, young people, men and women, and elders. Jeremiah 7 likewise announces wrath and fury poured upon the place, extending its list from people to livestock, trees and produce.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.

target_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, My wrath and fury are poured upon this place, upon the people and the livestock, upon every tree of their field and all the earth’s produce; and it will burn and not be extinguished.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel arrival of peoples summoned from distant extremities
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah announces a people from the north and nations roused from the earth's extremity. Isaiah likewise describes a signal raised among distant nations and a whistle from the earth's end for their rapid arrival; it does not repeat the northern direction.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.

target_units.text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: related metal-testing imagery for divine assessment
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: God declares that He has made the addressee a tester and speaks of testing the people's way, followed in context by metals and unsuccessful refining. Proverbs compares silver and gold tested in a furnace with hearts chosen before the Lord, giving a related assessment image while preserving its word chosen.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: I have made you a tester among tested peoples, and you will know Me when I test their way.

target_units.text: As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: contrast with the command to choose life
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah says they chose death rather than life in the account of judgment and dispersal. Deuteronomy sets the same alternatives before Israel and commands choosing life through love and obedience to God; Jeremiah describes the judged generation, whereas Deuteronomy exhorts those entering the land.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: because they chose death rather than life, and for all the remnants left from that generation in every place where I drive them away.

target_units.text: I call heaven and earth to witness unto you this day: I have set before your face life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, that you and your seed may live,

to love the Lord your God, to obey His voice, and to cleave unto Him; for this is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: contrast between rejecting divine speech and the foundation of wisdom
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah questions what wisdom remains in those who rejected the Lord's word. Proverbs places wisdom and perception in fear and reverence toward God and calls the ungodly despisers of wisdom and discipline, showing why rejection of divine instruction undermines a claim to wisdom.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: The wise were ashamed and terrified and captured, because they rejected the Lord’s word. What wisdom is in them?

target_units.text: The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.

final_amended_full_triples_reread.relationship: parallel tears flowing from the eyes over the people's shattering
final_amended_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah asks for a watery head and fountain-like eyes to weep day and night for the wounded people. Lamentations likewise describes the eye bringing down outpourings of water over the shattering of the people's daughter; the speaker then will not be silent because there is no recovery.
final_amended_full_triples_reread.source_text: Who will give my head water and my eyes a fountain of tears, and I will weep day and night for this people of Mine, for the wounded of the daughter of My people?

target_units.text: My eye will bring down outpourings of water at the shattering of the daughter of my people.
My eye was swallowed up, and I will not be silent, for there is no recovery,
until the Lord bends down and sees from heaven.

final_deferred_case_amendments_reread.source_text: A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
final_deferred_case_amendments_reread.reason: The unit speaks of a spirit of filling coming to the speaker while the speaker now announces judgments. Its precise image is unresolved in the supplied text; no target is retained on the basis of an assumed strong-wind reading.

reading_scope: All 225 complete actual native source units were read in exact order after the preceding Isaiah reading gate and the complete fresh Jeremiah inventory, before target curation. All 203 complete retained source-target-relationship-rationale triples were reread in five nontruncated batches, followed by 22 full amended or companion triples across 21 source references and the final additional 5:4 precision reread. The peer-requested category refinement at 4:16 was then read in its complete final triple; 23 distinct amended or companion triples across 22 source references are recorded. All 26 deferred source/reason cases and five complete read-unretained source-target/reason cases were reread, including the final 4:12 case correction. All 170 context ranges and 1162 distinct actual units were read this run. Pending cases receive zero completion credit; there are no unread hints. Composite Jeremiah 7:27–28 and native gaps remain intact. This is review of supplied native English, not original-language or every-tradition review.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit is only the introductory word-coming formula. The particular content of the commission is reviewed in the following units; another generic revelation formula would not provide a sufficiently particular connection for this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying, What do you see, Jeremiah? I said, A nut-wood staff.
deferred_source_units.reason: The supplied vision names a nut-wood staff. No verified counterpart establishes the significance of this particular object, and the performance promise in 1:12 does not justify substituting a familiar almond formulation or importing another staff narrative.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Hear the Lord’s word, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit summons Jacob and every Israelite clan to hear. Its particular indictment follows in 2:5; another broad summons to hear would mainly repeat an introductory form without a further supported connection.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully. See whether such things have happened.
deferred_source_units.reason: The command to inspect Kittim and Kedar introduces the comparison of exchanged gods in 2:11. No particular counterpart for this two-location investigation has been established, and the following supported comparison does not automatically complete this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes knew you and mocked you.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual verse says the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes knew and mocked the addressee. A parallel about Egypt shaving or breaking a crown would replace its supplied action; no precise counterpart to this named mockery is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: How will you say, I was not polluted and did not follow Baal? See your ways in the burial ground and know what you did. Late her voice wailed; her ways
deferred_source_units.reason: The denial of Baal pollution leads into a burial-ground reference and the unusual connected clause about a late-wailing voice and her ways. Read together with 2:24, these words do not support substituting the familiar camel imagery or assigning a secure particular counterpart to the complete unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: she broadened upon wilderness waters. In her soul’s desires she was carried by the wind; she was handed over. Who will turn her back? All who seek her will not toil; in her humiliation they will find her.
deferred_source_units.reason: The connected description speaks of broadened ways upon wilderness waters, desire, wind, being handed over and discovery in humiliation. No securely read target clarifies this full combination; familiar wild-donkey or mating-season wording is absent and cannot be substituted.

deferred_source_units.source_text: As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the sons of Israel will be ashamed: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests and their prophets.
deferred_source_units.reason: The particular comparison is shame like that of a caught thief, extended to Israel and its leaders. The read Proverbs thief passage concerns appetite and restitution rather than shame, while the Isaiah shame passage lacks the caught-thief comparison; both candidates remain unretained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Why do you speak to Me? All of you acted ungodly, and all of you acted lawlessly against Me, says the Lord.
deferred_source_units.reason: The question asks why the people speak to God and then charges everyone with ungodliness and lawlessness. No sufficiently particular counterpart to this question and accusation is established; a generic corporate confession would change the rhetorical situation.

deferred_source_units.source_text: What good practice will you still pursue in your ways to seek love? Not so; you too acted wickedly to pollute your ways.
deferred_source_units.reason: The rhetorical question about pursuing good practice to seek love is followed by polluted ways. The supplied phrasing does not warrant importing a claim that the woman teaches other evil women, and no precise target for its actual question is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Will He remain for ever, or will it be guarded always? Behold, you spoke and did these evil things and were able.
deferred_source_units.reason: The questions ask whether He remains forever or whether it is guarded always, without naming anger as the object. A target about anger not lasting forever would supply an unstated noun; the subsequent charge of effective evil does not resolve that wording sufficiently for a retained pair.

deferred_source_units.source_text: When you multiply and increase upon the land in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, The ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel. It will not come to mind, be named or be attended to, and it will not be made again.
deferred_source_units.reason: This unit specifically predicts the ark no longer being recalled, named, attended to or made again. General descriptions of the ark or a new covenant would not themselves establish this particular cessation claim; no verified direct counterpart is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: At that time they will say to this people and Jerusalem: A spirit of wandering in the wilderness; the daughter of My people’s way is not toward purity or holiness.
deferred_source_units.reason: The supplied image is a spirit of wandering in the wilderness and a way lacking purity or holiness. No definite counterpart is established, and a familiar hot wind used for winnowing would import absent wording.

deferred_source_units.source_text: A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit speaks of a spirit of filling coming to the speaker while the speaker now announces judgments. Its precise image is unresolved in the supplied text; no target is retained on the basis of an assumed strong-wind reading.

deferred_source_units.source_text: All are strong,
deferred_source_units.reason: The whole unit is All are strong, referring through context to the invading nation. A generic description of another strong army would add little beyond that broad military trait, so the actual short unit remains pending separately from supported 5:15 and 5:17.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Announce these things to the house of Jacob, and let it be heard in Judah.
deferred_source_units.reason: This is an announcement instruction to Jacob and Judah without the subsequent accusation itself. No particular connection beyond the generic two-house address has been retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Astonishment and horrifying things happened upon the land:
deferred_source_units.reason: This introductory line announces astonishment and horrifying things on the land. The particular corruption is specified in 5:31 and reviewed there; a general horror announcement would not independently substantiate this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: and your height will be taken away, daughter of Zion.
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual line says Zion will have her height taken away. No precise counterpart establishes the sense of this height in the siege setting, and familiar descriptions of a beautiful or luxuriant daughter are not present in this unit.

deferred_source_units.source_text: As a cistern cools water, so her evil cools; impiety and misery will be heard in her, continually before her. With pain and scourging
deferred_source_units.reason: The comparison says a cistern cools water and her evil cools, then continues into pain and scourging. No precise target clarifies this unusual cooling image; a spring constantly pouring out wickedness would substitute another wording.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Therefore the nations heard, and those shepherding their flocks.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit says nations and those shepherding their flocks heard, without specifying a separate response. The adjoining announcement in 6:19 is supported, but a broad appeal to nations would not establish a particular counterpart for this short hearing clause.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am placing weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will become weak in it; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.
deferred_source_units.reason: God places weakness upon the people, and fathers, sons and neighbors weaken or perish together. The supplied image is weakness rather than a stumbling stone; no distinct, sufficiently close counterpart to the combined formulation is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Hear the Lord’s word, all Judea!
deferred_source_units.reason: The actual unit is the brief summons for all Judea to hear the Lord. The ethical and temple-specific content follows in later units, and another generic hearing summons would not provide a particular connection for this one.

peer_requested_final_full_triples_reread.rationale: Jeremiah announces bands from a distant land raising their voice against Judah's cities. Isaiah likewise describes a signal among distant nations and their rapid, armed arrival, giving the military counterpart to the distant bands.
peer_requested_final_full_triples_reread.source_text: Remind the nations: Behold, they have come! Announce in Jerusalem: Bands come from a distant land and have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.

target_units.text: Therefore He will raise a signal among the distant nations and whistle to them from the earth’s end. Behold, they come quickly and lightly!
They will not hunger or grow weary, slumber or sleep, nor loosen the belts from their waists; their sandal straps will certainly not break.
Their arrows are sharp and their bows drawn. Their horses’ feet were reckoned like solid rock, and their chariot wheels like a storm.
They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.
